look_here_first: A small decumbent to ascending sharp-pod bundleflower: find 4–6 pairs of pinnae on a COMPLETE bipinnate leaf with a tiny cup-like extrafloral nectary beside the lowest pinnae. Heads have about 6–16 flowers (local descriptions vary); bisexual flowers with 10 stamens. Look for elongated pointed mature pods about 30–50 mm long. Critical comparison with accepted D. virgatus: do not use the historical name D. virgatus var. acuminatus as a separate species.

morphology_keys.growth_flower_fruit: Small sprawling to ascending perennial bundleflower in gravelly/sandy sites; heads relatively few-flowered; narrow pointed pods. Distinguish from broad sickle-podded Illinois bundleflower. Historically called Desmanthus virgatus var. acuminatus; treated here as an accepted species per ITIS.
morphology_keys.distinguishing_characters: A few-flowered head and pointed linear pod vs usually larger many-flowered heads of velutinus and illinoensis. D. virgatus may overlap in habits and narrow pod shapes; require well-fruited material and corroborating pinnae/stamen characters.
morphology_keys.shared_genus: Unarmed perennial Fabaceae with compound bipinnate leaves and small brushlike heads, often a petiolar/rachis gland, flat legume pods. Pod structure diagnostic.
morphology_keys.leaf: Helically alternate leaves with 4–6 pairs of primary pinnae; each pinna typically with 9–17 pairs of tiny leaflets; cup-like extrafloral nectary next to the proximal primary pinnae.
morphology_keys.flower: Headlike short axillary spike with approximately 6–16 flowers; lower often staminate, upper bisexual; bisexual flowers possess 10 free stamens.
morphology_keys.fruit: Narrow, acuminate, relatively straight mature pods commonly about 30–50 mm long. Measure actual specimens rather than relying only on habit.
morphology_keys.source_context: UT Austin Williamson County detailed voucher-based description, supplemented by Flora of North Central Texas

comparisons.key_distinctions: A few-flowered head and pointed linear pod vs usually larger many-flowered heads of velutinus and illinoensis. D. virgatus may overlap in habits and narrow pod shapes; require well-fruited material and corroborating pinnae/stamen characters.
